cities.name: Old Goa
cities.overview: Once the capital of Portuguese India and said to rival Lisbon in size, Old Goa is now a quiet collection of grand churches and convents beside the Mandovi River, 10 km from Panaji.

cities.name: Calangute
cities.overview: The busiest beach town in North Goa, with Candolim and Baga on either side. It is lined with shacks, water-sports operators and nightlife.

cities.name: Canacona
cities.overview: Goa's southernmost taluka, with quieter crescent beaches such as Palolem, Agonda and Patnem backed by palm groves and hills.

cities.name: Mollem
cities.overview: A village on the Goa–Karnataka border at the edge of Bhagwan Mahavir Wildlife Sanctuary, and the base for trips to Dudhsagar Falls.

cities.name: Panaji
cities.overview: Goa's small riverside capital on the Mandovi, with Portuguese lanes in Fontainhas and beaches at its edge.
cities.history: It became the capital of Portuguese India in 1843, replacing Old Goa, which had been abandoned after epidemics. It joined India with the rest of Goa in 1961.

cities.name: Margao
cities.overview: Goa's commercial capital in the south, and the base for the beaches and Portuguese-era houses of Salcete.

cities.name: Mapusa
cities.overview: North Goa's market town, and the road hub for the northern beaches and Anjuna.

cities.name: Ponda
cities.overview: Goa's temple country, inland among spice farms, where Hindu shrines moved during Portuguese rule.

cities.name: Vasco da Gama
cities.overview: A port town on the Mormugao peninsula, near the airport.

places.name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
places.shortDescription: A 16th-century baroque basilica that holds the remains of St Francis Xavier.
places.description: The Basilica of Bom Jesus is one of the oldest churches in India and its laterite façade has been left unplastered. Inside, a gilded altar and a carved marble tomb gifted by the Grand Duke of Tuscany hold the silver casket of St Francis Xavier. The saint's relics are displayed publicly once a decade, drawing pilgrims from across the world. Dress modestly and keep quiet during services.
places.history: Completed in 1605 by the Jesuits and raised to a minor basilica in 1946. It is part of the Churches and Convents of Goa UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed in 1986.
places.bestTimeNote: November to March. The Feast of St Francis Xavier falls on 3 December.

timings.hours: About 9:00 AM – 6:30 PM; opens later on Sundays for Mass

location.address: Old Goa Road, Bainguinim, Old Goa, Goa 403402

sources.title: Churches and Convents of Goa – UNESCO

images.alt: Basilica of Bom Jesus, Old Goa

places.name: Se Cathedral
places.shortDescription: One of the largest churches in Asia, dedicated to St Catherine and home of the 'Golden Bell'.
places.description: The Se Cathedral faces the Basilica of Bom Jesus across a wide lawn. Its plain Tuscan exterior opens onto a vast whitewashed nave and a gilded altar showing scenes from the life of St Catherine of Alexandria. Its tower holds the Golden Bell, one of the largest in Goa, named for its rich sound.
places.history: Built by the Portuguese to commemorate their capture of Goa on St Catherine's Day in 1510. Construction began in 1562 and the cathedral was completed in 1619.
highlights: Chapel of the Cross of Miracles

places.name: Calangute Beach
places.shortDescription: North Goa's 'Queen of Beaches', lined with shacks and packed with water sports.
places.description: Calangute is a long, wide stretch of sand that runs into Baga to the north and Candolim to the south. It is the place for parasailing, jet-skiing, banana boat rides and dolphin trips, followed by seafood at the beach shacks. It gets very crowded in the peak season; walk towards Candolim for a calmer stretch.
places.bestTimeNote: November to March. Water sports stop during the monsoon (June to September).

timings.hours: Open all day; swim only in flagged zones with lifeguards

places.name: Fort Aguada
places.shortDescription: A 17th-century Portuguese fort and lighthouse on a headland where the Mandovi River meets the sea.
places.description: Fort Aguada's laterite ramparts look out over Sinquerim Beach and the Arabian Sea. The upper fort holds a large freshwater cistern and a lighthouse, one of the oldest of its kind in Asia. The fort is best visited in the late afternoon for the sunset.
places.history: Built by the Portuguese in 1612 to guard against Dutch and Maratha attacks. Ships stopped here to take on fresh water from its springs, which gave the fort its name (aguada means 'watering place'). The lighthouse was added in 1864.

places.name: Palolem Beach
places.shortDescription: A calm crescent of white sand fringed by coconut palms in South Goa.
places.description: Palolem's sheltered bay is good for swimming and kayaking, and fishermen offer boat trips to see dolphins and to Butterfly Beach. Wooden beach huts line the sand during the season. Walk to the tidal Monkey Island at the north end at low tide, or try a 'silent disco' with headphones in the evening.
places.bestTimeNote: November to March; most beach huts close in the monsoon.

places.name: Dudhsagar Falls
places.shortDescription: A four-tiered, roughly 310-metre waterfall that looks like a stream of milk pouring down the Western Ghats.
places.description: Dudhsagar ('sea of milk') plunges down a forested cliff on the Mandovi River, with a railway bridge crossing its face. Visitors reach it by forest-department jeep safari from Collem through Bhagwan Mahavir Wildlife Sanctuary, followed by a short walk to the pool at its base. Wear sturdy shoes; the rocks are slippery.
places.bestTimeNote: October to January, when the falls are still full but jeep safaris are running. Safaris usually stop in peak monsoon.

entryFee.note: Jeep safari, entry and life-jacket fees apply; book at the Collem counter.

location.address: Bhagwan Mahavir Wildlife Sanctuary, Sanguem taluka, Goa 403410

places.name: Divar Island
places.shortDescription: A quiet river island of paddy fields, old Portuguese houses and village chapels, reached by a free ferry.
places.description: A five-minute ferry ride from Old Goa or Ribandar takes you to Divar, where life moves at village pace. Cycle or drive through rice fields and mangroves, past colourful Portuguese-era homes, up to the hilltop Church of Our Lady of Compassion for views over the Mandovi. In August the island celebrates Bonderam, a festival with floats and drums.
places.history: Divar was an important Hindu pilgrimage site before the Portuguese arrived; the original Saptakoteshwar temple stood here before it was moved inland in the 16th century.
places.bestTimeNote: October to February; August for the Bonderam festival.

entryFee.note: The ferry is free for foot passengers.

timings.hours: Ferries run frequently from early morning to late evening

location.address: Divar Island, Tiswadi, North Goa, Goa 403403

places.name: Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception Church
places.shortDescription: The white zigzag-stair church above Panaji's main square, first built in 1541.
places.description: A brilliant white Portuguese Baroque church reached by a criss-cross staircase, right in the centre of town. Sailors once stopped here on arrival from Lisbon.
places.history: First built in 1541 as a chapel, it was later rebuilt.

sources.title: Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception Church, Goa – Wikipedia

images.alt: Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception Church, Panaji

places.name: Reis Magos Fort
places.shortDescription: A restored Portuguese fort on the north bank of the Mandovi, opposite Panaji.
places.description: A small red fort with views across the river to the capital. It has been restored and now has a small exhibition on Goa's history.

places.name: Miramar Beach
places.shortDescription: Panaji's city beach, where the Mandovi meets the Arabian Sea, popular for sunset walks.
places.description: A wide golden beach a short ride from the city centre, with views of Fort Aguada across the river. It's best for walks, not swimming.

places.name: Dona Paula
places.shortDescription: A headland at the meeting of the Zuari and Mandovi, with a viewpoint and water sports.
places.description: A jetty and viewpoint between two rivers, close to the National Institute of Oceanography. It's a good spot for the sunset and for water sports.

places.name: Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A mangrove bird sanctuary on Chorão Island, on the Mandovi, named after the great ornithologist.
places.description: A boat trip through the mangroves shows kingfishers, herons and mudskippers. Take the free ferry from Ribandar, and get there early.

places.name: Chapora Fort
places.shortDescription: The Dil Chahta Hai fort, an Adil Shahi site rebuilt by the Portuguese, high over Vagator.
places.description: Crumbling red walls on a hill, with a wide view of the Chapora River and the northern beaches. It's become a popular place to go at sunset.
places.history: Built by Adil Shah as Shahpoora, and rebuilt by the Portuguese in 1617.

places.name: Anjuna Beach
places.shortDescription: A rocky beach in Bardez, with a famous Wednesday flea market and a history of hippie travel.
places.description: Rocks and coves, with a big weekly flea market in season and beach shacks. It's been a centre of Goa's hippie and party scene since the 1960s.

places.name: Vagator Beach
places.shortDescription: Red cliffs and a small beach in North Goa, below Chapora Fort.
places.description: Red laterite cliffs drop to the sand, with a carved face in the rocks at Little Vagator. It's quieter than Baga and has a good sunset.

places.name: Baga Beach
places.shortDescription: North Goa's liveliest beach, with water sports, nightclubs and Baga Creek at one end.
places.description: Busy beach shacks and water sports by day, with clubs on Tito's Lane by night. It's a loud and popular stretch, 2 km north of Calangute.

places.name: Candolim Beach
places.shortDescription: A long, quieter beach just south of Calangute, running down to Fort Aguada.
places.description: A wide beach with plenty of shacks and fewer crowds than Baga. The wreck of the River Princess was a landmark here for years.

places.name: Arambol Beach
places.shortDescription: Goa's northern hippie village beach, with a sweet water lake, drum circles and paragliding.
places.description: A long beach with yoga, music and a small freshwater lake just behind the headland. Paragliders launch from the cliffs in the north.

places.name: Morjim Beach
places.shortDescription: A beach in Pernem, on the Chapora estuary, and a nesting site for Olive Ridley turtles.
places.description: A broad, quiet beach that's protected for nesting turtles in winter. Many Russian visitors stay here, and it's also a kite-surfing spot.

places.name: Fort Tiracol
places.shortDescription: A Portuguese fort at Goa's northern tip, on the Terekhol River, now a heritage hotel.
places.description: A small fort with a chapel, reached by a short ferry from Querim. It's right at the Maharashtra border, with big sea views.
places.history: A key site of the 1955 Satyagraha against Portuguese rule.

places.name: Colva Beach
places.shortDescription: A 2.5 km stretch of white sand in Salcete, the most popular beach in South Goa.
places.description: Fine sand and coconut palms, with an easy bus from Margao. It's busy with Indian holiday-makers at weekends, and water sports are available.

places.name: Benaulim Beach
places.shortDescription: A calm beach in South Goa, quieter than Colva, in a village of old Portuguese houses.
places.description: A calm, wide beach with fishing boats and slow-paced shacks. The Goa Chitra museum of Goan life is in the village.

places.name: Braganza House
places.shortDescription: A grand 17th-century Portuguese-era mansion in Chandor, still lived in by the same family.
places.description: A long facade hides halls of Chinese porcelain, rosewood furniture and a ballroom. Two wings are owned by different branches of the family, and guided tours are by donation.

places.name: Agonda Beach
places.shortDescription: A quiet, long beach in Canacona, one of four turtle nesting sites under Indian coastal rules.
places.description: A long, unspoiled stretch of sand with low-key huts. It's a great place to slow down, with Olive Ridley turtles in season.

places.name: Cabo de Rama Fort
places.shortDescription: An old hillfort on a high cape in Canacona, with a small church and wide sea views.
places.description: Crumbling walls, an old cannon and a white chapel on a windy headland. Few people come here, and it's great at sunset.

places.name: Cotigao Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A forest sanctuary in Canacona, established in 1968, known for treetop watchtowers.
places.description: Goa's second largest sanctuary, with tall forest and a treetop tower to watch wildlife. Go early, as most animals are hard to see later on.

places.name: Bhagwan Mahaveer Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A 240 sq km forest reserve in Goa's Western Ghats, around Dudhsagar and Tambdi Surla.
places.description: Goa's largest protected area, on the Karnataka border, with gaur, hornbills and the Devil's Canyon gorge. It's also home to the Dudhsagar Falls.

sources.title: Bhagwan Mahaveer Sanctuary and Mollem National Park – Wikipedia

places.name: Mahadev Temple, Tambdi Surla
places.shortDescription: A small 13th-century stone Shiva temple deep in the Goan forest, the state's oldest temple.
places.description: A black basalt Kadamba temple that survived because it was hidden in the forest. It's a beautifully carved building, in a clearing beside a stream.
places.history: Built in the Kadamba period, around the 13th century.

places.name: Bondla Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: Goa's smallest sanctuary, 7.98 sq km, with a mini zoo, deer park and botanical garden.
places.description: A small park that's good for families, with a small zoo and a nature trail in the Western Ghats foothills.

places.name: Shri Mangueshi Temple
places.shortDescription: A large white Shiva temple at Mangueshi in Ponda, 21 km from Panaji, with a tall lamp tower.
places.description: A distinctive white temple with a domed roof, a Goan blend of styles, and a seven-storey lamp tower. Its deity was moved inland during Portuguese rule.

places.name: Naval Aviation Museum
places.shortDescription: A military aviation museum at Bogmalo, 6 km from Vasco, with old Indian Navy aircraft.
places.description: Retired aircraft stand outside, while the galleries indoors cover uniforms and naval flying history. It's one of the few military aviation museums in India.

images.alt: Naval Aviation Museum, Vasco da Gama
